watchordr.summaryText: A teenager swallows a cursed object and is pulled into a world of sorcerers who fight monsters born from human negativity. Four entries so far: three TV seasons and one prequel film. Here is the order to watch them in, and why the film does not go first.

entries.title: Jujutsu Kaisen
entries.note: Start here. All 24 episodes introduce Yuji Itadori, the world of curses, and the sorcerers who fight them. Nothing else in the series makes sense without it.

entries.title: Jujutsu Kaisen 0
entries.note: A prequel film following Yuta Okkotsu, set about a year before Season 1. Watch it after Season 1 rather than first: the film assumes you already understand how curses and jujutsu sorcerers work, and its closing scene lands only if you have seen the TV series. Several characters introduced here become important in Season 2 and Season 3.

entries.title: Jujutsu Kaisen Season 2
entries.note: 23 episodes, split into two halves. The first five are a flashback to Gojo and Geto's student years, which explains most of what Jujutsu Kaisen 0 only hinted at. The rest covers the Shibuya Incident, the turning point of the whole series.

entries.title: Jujutsu Kaisen Season 3: The Culling Game Part 1
entries.note: 12 episodes picking up immediately after Season 2. The opening episodes deal with the fallout of the Shibuya Incident before the Culling Game itself begins, so the setup will not make sense without Season 2 fresh in mind.
entries.warning: ⚠ The anime currently ends here. A second part covering the rest of the Culling Game arc has been announced, but no broadcast date has been confirmed.
entries.matchedCatalogueTitle: JUJUTSU KAISEN Season 3: The Culling Game Part 1

watchordr.summaryText: Humanity lives walled in against giant man-eating Titans, and the fight to survive slowly turns into the discovery of what the world outside the walls really is. The anime runs to 87 TV episodes across four seasons, plus two feature-length specials that close the story and eight optional side-story episodes. It adapts the manga through to its final chapter.

entries.title: Attack on Titan
entries.note: Start here. 25 episodes covering the fall of the wall, the training corps and the Female Titan arc. Everything later grows out of these episodes.

entries.title: Attack on Titan Season 2
entries.note: 12 episodes, picking up immediately after Season 1. Short, but this is where the first major answers about the Titans arrive.

entries.title: Attack on Titan Season 3
entries.note: 12 episodes. The focus moves inside the walls and onto who has been running things. Ends mid-story and leads straight into Part 2.

entries.title: Attack on Titan Season 3 Part 2
entries.note: 10 episodes. The direct continuation of Season 3 — the two cours are one season split by a broadcast gap, so watch them back to back.

entries.title: Attack on Titan Final Season
entries.note: 16 episodes, and the first one drops you somewhere new with a cast you have never met. Give it four or five episodes before judging it.
entries.warning: ⚠ The opening episodes deliberately withhold the connection to the previous season. The shift in setting and perspective is the point, not a mistake.

entries.title: Attack on Titan Final Season Part 2
entries.note: 12 episodes continuing straight on from the previous part. The two halves were made as one season and split across a year.
entries.matchedCatalogueTitle: Attack on Titan Final Season Part 2

entries.title: Attack on Titan Final Season THE FINAL CHAPTERS Special 1
entries.note: A single feature-length episode of about an hour, not a recap or a preview. In Japan the two specials were also released in weekly episode form, continuing the Final Season's numbering past episode 87.
entries.matchedCatalogueTitle: Attack on Titan Final Season THE FINAL CHAPTERS Special 1

entries.title: Attack on Titan Final Season THE FINAL CHAPTERS Special 2
entries.note: The ending, running about 85 minutes. Watch it straight after Special 1 — the two together are the conclusion of the whole series.
entries.matchedCatalogueTitle: Attack on Titan Final Season THE FINAL CHAPTERS Special 2

entries.title: Attack on Titan OVA
entries.note: Three self-contained episodes bundled with manga volumes 12, 13 and 14. All three take place during the cadet days, between episodes 3 and 4 of Season 1, and none of them touch the main plot.

entries.title: Attack on Titan: No Regrets
entries.note: Two episodes about Levi before he joined the Survey Corps, bundled with manga volumes 15 and 16. The best of the side stories, and it works far better once you already know him.

entries.title: Attack on Titan: Lost Girls
entries.note: Three episodes: a two-part Annie story set between episodes 16 and 17 of Season 1, and a Mikasa story tied to the events of episode 49. The Mikasa episode is the most detached from canon of anything here.

recommendedOrder.warning: ⚠ The opening episodes deliberately withhold the connection to the previous season. The shift in setting and perspective is the point, not a mistake.

recommendedOrder.title: Attack on Titan Final Season Part 2
recommendedOrder.note: 12 episodes continuing straight on from the previous part. The two halves were made as one season and split across a year.
recommendedOrder.matchedCatalogueTitle: Attack on Titan Final Season Part 2

recommendedOrder.title: Attack on Titan Final Season THE FINAL CHAPTERS Special 1
recommendedOrder.note: A single feature-length episode of about an hour, not a recap or a preview. In Japan the two specials were also released in weekly episode form, continuing the Final Season's numbering past episode 87.
recommendedOrder.matchedCatalogueTitle: Attack on Titan Final Season THE FINAL CHAPTERS Special 1

recommendedOrder.title: Attack on Titan Final Season THE FINAL CHAPTERS Special 2
recommendedOrder.note: The ending, running about 85 minutes. Watch it straight after Special 1 — the two together are the conclusion of the whole series.
recommendedOrder.matchedCatalogueTitle: Attack on Titan Final Season THE FINAL CHAPTERS Special 2

recommendedOrder.title: Attack on Titan OVA
recommendedOrder.note: Three self-contained episodes bundled with manga volumes 12, 13 and 14. All three take place during the cadet days, between episodes 3 and 4 of Season 1, and none of them touch the main plot.

recommendedOrder.title: Attack on Titan: No Regrets
recommendedOrder.note: Two episodes about Levi before he joined the Survey Corps, bundled with manga volumes 15 and 16. The best of the side stories, and it works far better once you already know him.

recommendedOrder.title: Attack on Titan: Lost Girls
recommendedOrder.note: Three episodes: a two-part Annie story set between episodes 16 and 17 of Season 1, and a Mikasa story tied to the events of episode 49. The Mikasa episode is the most detached from canon of anything here.
